Read and check a GLOW configuration

Source: R/glow_config_read.R
read_glow_config.Rd

Resolves a YAML configuration against the base configuration and the settings registry. A user file holds only the settings that differ from the base. Its extends line names the file it builds on, and a file without that line builds on the base, so configurations form a chain that ends at the base.

read_glow_config(config = NULL, base, registry, root = ".")

Arguments

config

Path of the user's YAML configuration, or NULL to resolve the base alone.

base

Path of the base configuration (base_config.yml), which sets every registered setting.

registry

Path of the settings registry (settings-registry.yml), which gives every setting its section, type and default.

root

Directory from which a relative data path of the configuration is meant. It is recorded with the result and not used to read the configuration files themselves. Default: the working directory.

Value

An object of class glow_config: a list with the top-level settings (such as dataset) and one list per section (such as snv_set), every value converted to its registered type. A setting that is null is present with the value NULL. A setting of type r_function is an R function whose source text is in the attribute glow_source. The attributes glow_chain (the files read, base first, with their checksums), glow_registry (the registry as read, with the type, the derived mark and the old name of every setting) and glow_root record where the settings came from.

Details

Algorithm:

  1. Read the registry and check that every default is valid under its type.

  2. Follow the chain: the user file, the file its extends names (read relative to the file that contains the line), and so on to the base. Files are compared by their real paths, so a cycle is found. A file may name the base by its bare file name from any folder.

  3. Check each file on its own: a section or a setting that the registry does not hold is an error, with the nearest registered name, and so is a value that cannot be read as the type of its setting, even when a later file of the chain replaces it.

  4. Merge from the base toward the user file. Sections merge setting by setting, and a setting that is a map with declared fields merges field by field, unless the registry marks it replace_whole. Every other value (a scalar, a list, a map with free keys, a value that takes one of several forms) replaces the inherited value whole. An explicit null replaces the inherited value. A section with nothing after its colon sets nothing.

  5. Convert each value by its registered type.

Every scalar is read as the text the user wrote and converted by the registered type of its setting, so no stays text for a text setting, 1e6 is a number for a numeric one, and 010 is ten. A logical takes true or false. A list of integers may be written as a range, 1-22.

Problems of names and types are collected and reported in one error, each with the file it is in. A file that cannot be found or parsed, and a cycle, stop the function at once.

Assumptions: the function checks the structure and the types of a configuration and nothing else. It does not check that a path exists, and it does not fill a null that a later step derives. A setting of type r_function is parsed and never run. The function it returns has the global environment, so, when a step calls it later, it sees base R and the attached packages and nothing of the configuration; a function that depends on other objects of the session is not reproducible from the configuration alone.

Computational complexity: linear in the number of settings and files.

See also

write_resolved_config, write_base_config

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
cfg <- read_glow_config("cohort0203.yml",
                        base = "base-config/base_config.yml",
                        registry = "base-config/settings-registry.yml")
cfg$dataset
cfg$snv_set$ld_threshold
} # }
